kaps_punt: Khoikhoi Herdersamelewing in die Later Steentydperk - Herderlike leefwyse | Hoe San en Khoikhoi dieselfde grond gedeel het

items.bewering: Die San het al baie lank as jagter-versamelaars in Suider-Afrika geleef. Hulle het wild gejag en veldkos versamel.
items.bron: Sadr, 'The story of how livestock made its way to southern Africa', The Conversation / Wits (2016): Later Stone Age hunting and gathering was in place before livestock arrived and remained the main way of life; Kyoto University Central Kalahari San studies (repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp) on San hunting and gathering.

items.bewering: Sowat 2 000 jaar gelede het mense hier in die Later Steentydperk ook begin om vee aan te hou.
items.bron: Sadr, The Conversation / Wits (2016): earliest sheep in the last few centuries BC; Wits/heritagedaily summary: earliest sheep and cattle in southern Africa about 2 000 years ago; SAHO 'Prehistory of the Cape Town area': first domestic animals in deposits dating to about 2 000 years ago. The lesson does not claim the Khoikhoi were the very first herders, so the debate over whether Khoe speakers came with the first sheep or a little later does not touch this sentence.

items.bewering: Die Khoikhoi was sulke mense, en hulle het beeste en skape gehad.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (sahistory.org.za/people-south-africa/khoikhoi, encyclopaedic page, not a classroom page); SAHO 'Prehistory of the Cape Town area': Khoe pastoralists with cattle and sheep.

items.bewering: Ons noem hulle herders (veewagters), want hulle het hul diere opgepas en versorg.
items.bron: 'Veewagter' as established Afrikaans for someone who herds livestock: Afrikaanse Bybel 1933/53 (Bybelgenootskap van Suid-Afrika), Genesis 13:7 'die veewagters van Abram en die veewagters van Lot' (bible.com GEN.13.AFR53), and NLV Genesis 13:8 'ons veewagters'.

items.bewering: Baie San het steeds soos voorheen van jag en versamel geleef.
items.bron: Sadr, The Conversation (2016): 'Hunting and gathering remained the main subsistence activity despite the availability of livestock'.

items.bewering: 'n Trop beeste eet elke dag baie gras en drink baie water.
items.blok: Op soek na gras en water
items.bron: NMSU Guide B-231 'Estimating Water Intake for Range Beef Cattle' (cow eats about 2.5% of body weight in dry matter a day); Beef Research Council Canada, water for beef cattle (roughly 30-78 litres a day per animal).

items.bewering: Na 'n ruk was die gras op een plek klaar opgevreet. Dan moes die herders verder trek. Hulle het hul kampe opgebreek en saam met die vee na nuwe weiding geloop. Waar daar genoeg gras en water was, het hulle weer 'n kamp opgeslaan. So het die Khoikhoi met hul vee deur die land rondgetrek.
items.blok: Op soek na gras en water
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': 'They moved according to the seasons and only stayed in one place for a few weeks', possessions easy to carry; Khoekhoe described as transhumant pastoralists whose portable huts were taken down and re-erected when surrounding grazing was depleted (Khoekhoe encyclopaedic entries); Smith & Ouzman (2004) note herder sites cluster near water the herds needed.

items.bewering: Die koeie het melk gegee, en melk was 'n belangrike kos vir die Khoikhoi.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': women milked the animals, and wealthier people shared milk with poorer members; Khoekhoe encyclopaedic entries: cattle milk an essential part of the diet. (Ewes were also milked; the lesson does not deny it.)

items.bewering: Die diere het ook vleis gegee.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': cattle were slaughtered for major ceremonies and cattle that died were eaten; Khoekhoe encyclopaedic entries: sheep were slaughtered more often. True as written. Note for a person, not a fault: cattle were seldom killed for everyday food, so the sentence must not be expanded into one saying the Khoikhoi lived mainly on beef.

items.bewering: Die Khoikhoi het ook nog gejag en veldkos versamel, maar hul vee was hul rykdom.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': 'The women milked the animals and gathered wild plants from the veld and the men killed game for everyday food'; animals 'were a sign of wealth'.

items.bewering: Die vee het aan 'n gesin of 'n persoon behoort en nie aan die hele groep nie. 'n Gesin met 'n groot trop was ryk, en 'n gesin met min diere was arm.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': 'Khoikhoi society consisted of both rich and poor, as animals - which were a sign of wealth - could belong to individuals.' (Land/territory was held communally, but the lesson speaks only of the livestock, which is correct.)

items.bewering: Dit was anders as by die San. Die San het die vleis van 'n jagtog met die hele groep gedeel.
items.bron: Wiessner & Huang, PNAS (Ju/'hoansi): obligatory meat sharing after a successful hunt; Lee's Ju/'hoansi ethnography as summarised by UNCG Peaceful Societies: sharing extends to everyone in the camp; SAHO 'Khoikhoi': the San 'were all considered equal and shared everything', in contrast with Khoikhoi rich and poor.

items.bewering: Die San was jagter-versamelaars, en die Khoikhoi was herders. Albei het rondgetrek, maar om verskillende redes.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (Khoikhoi moved with the seasons for grazing); Kyoto University Central Kalahari studies (San moved frequently to obtain bush foods).

items.bewering: Die San het getrek om wild en veldkos te volg namate die seisoene verander het.
items.bron: Kyoto University studies of the Gui and Gana San (repository.kulib.kyoto-u.ac.jp): gathering activity varies with the seasonal changes and people acquired bush foods by moving frequently; game concentrates near remaining water in the dry months.

items.bewering: Die Khoikhoi het getrek om gras en water vir hul vee te vind.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi'; Khoekhoe encyclopaedic entries describing transhumance tied to water and grazing.

items.bewering: Albei groepe het tale met klikklanke gepraat, maar dit was verskillende tale.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': both used clicks; the Khoikhoi spoke closely related dialects while the San spoke more divergent languages; Guldemann, ''Khoisan' linguistic classification today' (Benjamins, CILT 330): Khoe-Kwadi is a separate lineage from Kx'a and Tuu, so 'Khoisan' is not one language family; Britannica: clicks are a regular part of the consonant system in these languages.

items.bewering: Mense noem hulle soms saam die Khoisan. Dit is 'n versamelnaam vir albei, maar nie almal is dit eens oor hierdie naam nie.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoisan identity' (sahistory.org.za/article/khoisan-identity): term coined by Leonhard Schultze in 1928 as a collective label for herders and hunter-gatherers; San representatives (2003, with WIMSA) objected to being grouped under it and prefer community names or 'San', or 'Khoe-San'; Guldemann on its linguistic inaccuracy.

items.bewering: Navorsers is dit ook nie eens oor hoe skerp ons die San en die Khoikhoi van mekaar kan onderskei nie.
items.bron: Sadr, 'Invisible herders? The archaeology of Khoekhoe pastoralists', Southern African Humanities: Later Stone Age material culture does not show the language of its users; Oudepost excavation: the boundary between Khoekhoe and hunter-gatherers 'was not as impermeable as previously assumed'; Elphick's model of a fluid division between herders and hunters (summarised in UCT thesis material); Barnard, 'Ethnographic analogy and the reconstruction of early Khoekhoe society', Southern African Humanities.

items.bewering: Die San en die Khoikhoi het dikwels in dieselfde dele van die land geleef. Soms het hulle vreedsaam naby mekaar gewoon. Hulle het dan handel gedryf en dinge met mekaar geruil.
items.bron: Ostrich eggshell bead studies of Cape sites (Die Krans, Witklip; citing A.B. Smith): goods transferred from herders to hunters and hunters drawn into the herders' economic ambit; Denbow (1984), 'Prehistoric herders and foragers of the Kalahari: the evidence for 1500 years of interaction'; Barnard on Khoisan exchange relations; Smith & Ouzman (2004): Khoekhoen and San images overlap at the same sites.

items.bewering: Maar veral in droë jare was water en weiding op baie plekke skaars.
items.bron: Kyoto University Central Kalahari studies: droughts last many months and waterholes dry up; Elphick's model (via UCT thesis material and SAHO): herders could lose their herds through drought.

items.bewering: Die herders se vee het dieselfde water en gras nodig gehad as die wild wat die San gejag het. As daar te min vir almal was, het die groepe soms daaroor gebots. Die verhouding was dus nie altyd vreedsaam nie en ook nie altyd vyandig nie.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoikhoi': differences in way of life led to 'misunderstandings and subsequent conflict between the two groups'; grazing game (zebra, wildebeest, antelope) and cattle use the same pasture and water; Smith & Ouzman (2004) on herder sites near water; Barnard (Southern African Humanities) on shifts between hunting and herding and their interaction; together with the exchange evidence above, both halves of 'not always peaceful, not always hostile' are supported.

items.bewering: Baie San-rotskuns wys prente van mense en diere.
items.bron: Smith & Ouzman, 'Taking Stock: Identifying Khoekhoen Herder Rock Art in Southern Africa', Current Anthropology 45 (2004), and Wits Makgabeng thesis: San fine-line art is naturalistic images of people and animals, contrasted with the geometric herder tradition.

items.bewering: Op sommige plekke vind ons egter 'n ander soort rotskuns. Dit bestaan meestal uit geometriese patrone, soos sirkels, kolle en lyne.
items.bron: Smith & Ouzman (2004), abstract (repository.up.ac.za handle 2263/14121): a tradition 'dominated by rough-pecked and finger-painted geometric motifs'; academic summaries list circles, divided circles, dots, rows of dots and lines.

items.bewering: Navorsers verbind hierdie patrone met vroeë herders.
items.bron: Smith & Ouzman (2004) concluded the tradition was predominantly Khoekhoen herder art; Wits Rock Art Research Institute, 'Herder arts of Africa': 'possibly arriving with herders', with the caution that it may not have stayed only with ethnic Khoe. The lesson's verb 'verbind' states the attribution as researchers' view, not settled fact, which matches the sources.

items.bewering: herder: Iemand wat vee aanhou en oppas, soos beeste en skape.
items.bron: Consistent with the usage in SAHO 'Khoikhoi' (herders kept and moved with cattle and sheep) and AFR53 Genesis 13:7 'veewagters'.

items.bewering: vee: Diere wat mense in troppe aanhou, soos beeste en skape.
items.bron: Afrikaans livestock usage in Senwes 'Voedingwenke vir veeboere tydens droogte' (2015), where 'veeboere' keep beeste and skape; SAHO 'Khoikhoi' herds of cattle and sheep.

items.bewering: weiding: Gras en ander plante in die veld wat vee kan eet.
items.bron: Senwes 'Voedingwenke vir veeboere tydens droogte' (2015) uses 'tipe weiding' and 'wei-radius' for the veld vegetation grazed by livestock; Dutch cognate 'weiden' = let livestock graze on land (dbnl.org).

items.bewering: jagter-versamelaar: Iemand wat kos kry deur wilde diere te jag en veldkos te versamel.
items.bron: Kyoto University Central Kalahari studies (San obtain food by hunting and gathering bush foods); Sadr, The Conversation (2016).

items.bewering: rykdom: Die waardevolle dinge wat 'n persoon of 'n gesin besit.
items.bron: Ordinary meaning, consistent with SAHO 'Khoikhoi' use of animals as 'a sign of wealth' owned by individuals; no conflict with the lesson's use.

items.bewering: Khoisan: 'n Naam wat soms vir die San en die Khoikhoi saam gebruik word, al het hulle op verskillende maniere geleef.
items.bron: SAHO 'Khoisan identity': collective term coined by Schultze (1928) for Khoi pastoralists and San hunter-gatherers. Read alone, the entry is true; the dispute over the name is carried by the study block.

items.bewering: versamelnaam: 'n Naam wat vir verskeie groepe of dinge saam gebruik word.
items.bron: Ordinary meaning of a collective name, matching how SAHO 'Khoisan identity' describes 'Khoisan' as a collective label.

items.bewering: klikklank: 'n Klapgeluid, meestal met die tong gemaak, wat in sommige tale deel van woorde is.
items.bron: Britannica, 'click (speech sound)': a suction sound made in the mouth, a regular part of the consonant system of languages such as Nama and !Xoo; Britannica Kids: made with the tongue against the roof of the mouth. 'Meestal' correctly leaves room for the bilabial click, made with the lips.

items.bewering: geometriese patrone: Patrone wat uit lyne en eenvoudige vorms bestaan, soos sirkels en kolle.
items.bron: Matches the motifs listed for the geometric herder tradition in Smith & Ouzman (2004) and related academic summaries (circles, dots, lines).

opsomming: Al 33 nagaanbare bewerings is teen bronne bevestig en die les bevat geen oortreffende trap of analogie nie, met net een waarskuwing vir later hersienings: 'Die diere het ook vleis gegee' is waar, maar die Khoikhoi het beeste selde vir gewone kos geslag, so die sin moet nie uitgebrei word tot 'hulle het van beesvleis geleef' nie.
